QuestInfo.name: Words Nobody Taught
QuestInfo.0: #b#p715##k has something she wants to share.
QuestInfo.1: #b#p715##k can't read her grandmother's journal. It's written in the old fairy script. Take the #b#t4031140##k to #b#p712##k in #b#m010006160##k.
QuestInfo.2: I brought the #b#t4031140##k to #b#p712##k. He recognized the old script right away.

0.0: My grandmother, #bElda#k, was a hearthkeeper. Long ago, when the cave fairies lived in the deep halls, a hearthkeeper kept the fires and remembered the names of everyone who had passed on.
0.1: When the others left the deep halls, she stayed behind. I was very small. She never came back up, and no one would tell me why.
0.2: All I have is this #b#t4031140##k. But it's written in the old script, and no one has taught it since we moved. I can't read a single word.
0.3: #b#p712##k in #b#m010006160##k studies our old ways. Would you take it to him? It's a long way down, so please be careful.

yes.0: Here it is. Please don't lose it! #b#p712##k is in #b#m010006160##k, deep in the tunnels.

no.0: I understand. It's a long way down. I'll keep the journal safe until you're ready.

1.0: A journal written in the old hearthkeeper script? I haven't seen one of these in years! May I?
1.1: ...This belonged to #bElda#k? I remember the name. The hearthkeepers wrote in this script so their records would outlast them.
1.2: Most of it is a list of names: the fairies she laid to rest in the old tomb, one name for every winter. But the last pages describe the #bLantern Rite#k.

npc.0: #b#p712##k is in #b#m010006160##k. Please take him the #b#t4031140##k.

item.0: You said you had a journal for me? I don't see it with you. If it's lost, #b#p715##k may know what to do.

lost.0: You lost the journal?! ...Oh. Wait. My grandmother kept a copy. Hearthkeepers always kept two.
lost.1: Here. Please take it to #b#p712##k in #b#m010006160##k.
